title: Canonical reconstructed exceptional-system counit and its transpose
statement: Fix the prime, positive-characteristic base field, finite-type separated schemes, morphism and compactification, with the normalized ordinary reconstruction context of [def-pur-exceptional-reconstruction-context]. A supplied exceptional datum consists of an integral constructible input L, an actual ordinary derived pro-etale strict coefficient system M, and its specified level isomorphisms to the finite exceptional images of the reductions of L. Define its Brown tower and counit using the specified site adjunctions. Require normalization and coefficient-transition compatibility. The alternatives retain either the specified whole-system isomorphism to the Brown tower, or one integer degree containing every level's cohomology. Require a common finite cohomological interval and intrinsic finite-stratification constructibility [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and require the actual total limit to be integral constructible with invertible reduction counit. Given an actual Brown-system identification and the invertible site and reduction units, define the reconstructed integral counit by applying the actual total limit and inverse reduction unit. Realize and rationalize it using [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], then extend to the finite-subfield-valued closure coefficient and precompose with the inverse specified projection comparison. Define the exceptional comparison to be its adjunction transpose for the exact chosen bounded constructible condensed adjunction [sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek]. A conclusion datum retains the whole-system identification, its evaluations, the required boundedness and unit isomorphisms, and invertibility of this particular transpose. This definition asserts no existence or invertibility theorem.
